<pr_description>
Consider the following PR description:
SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

</pr_description>

Let me analyze this PR description. The issue is about `SplitArrayField` with `BooleanField` in Django. When there's a `SplitArrayField` containing `BooleanField` widgets, once a `True` value is encountered, all subsequent widgets are shown as checked even if their actual values are `False`.

The problem is identified as being in the `CheckboxInput` widget's `get_context()` method which modifies the `attrs` dict passed into it, specifically setting `attrs['checked'] = True`.

import sys

from django.forms.widgets import CheckboxInput

print("  PASS")

print("  PASS")

print("  PASS")

assert has_class == True, "FAIL: should have class"
assert 'checked' not in original_attrs, "FAIL: original attrs should not have checked"
print("  PASS")

# Test 6: attrs with existing keys, value=False

assert has_class == True, "FAIL: should have class"
assert 'checked' not in original_attrs, "FAIL: original attrs should not have checked"
print("  PASS")

# Test 7: Verify multiple calls don't affect each other
print("\nTest 7: Multiple calls with alternating True/False values")
values = [True, False, True, False, True]
expected_checked = [True, False, True, False, True]

for i, (val, expected) in enumerate(zip(values, expected_checked)):
    ctx = widget.get_context(f'field_{i}', val, shared_attrs)
    checked = ctx['widget']['attrs'].get('checked', False)
    assert checked == expected, f"FAIL at index {i}: expected {expected}, got {checked}"
    assert 'checked' not in shared_attrs, f"FAIL: shared attrs was modified at index {i}"

print(f"  All {len(values)} calls correct, shared_attrs unchanged: {shared_attrs}")
print("  PASS")

print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("All edge case tests PASSED!")
EOF
